searchText: What additional permissions? Hmm, is there no way to do it from the action itself? Feels like hitting the API isn't the right solution here. This is how you would do it from within an action. ```ts import { getOctokit } from '@actions/github' getOctokit(process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN).rest.issues.createComment({ owner, repo, issueNumber, body }) ``` And I don't *think* it requires any additional permissions? I'm kind of liking dragging this out, because it makes it so the number gets stickier before we change it, to further break things for the authors. I have never before considered a coup to take over the EIP editing process, but stopping favoritism/favor trading/backroom deals is apparently the thing that may turn me into an illegitimate dictator. That looks exactly like what I'm doing: https://github.com/SamWilsn/eipw-action/blob/05f5d561028480a566b756424fa2c657268897b5/src/main.ts#L116-L124 Hmm... I think the action has read only permission https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/settings/actions at the bottom, I think. I think you overestimate my participation in this, and am a little offended you're saying I participated in collusion. Not to throw Matt under the bus too much, and perhaps what I said could have been interpreted as consenting, but that was certainly not my intent: > /me just applies the rules as I understand them. > Do whatever [...] > I don't really care if people snipe, but I firmly believe in consistency > And I _seem_ to remember that Micah had renumbered an EIP that had sniped a number > You have the same authority as I do, so if you want to give them 5000, go for it 😛 > I just don't think it's fair. The conversation this excerpt is from took place on the 29th, and I had no idea the EIP would be merged as 5000 two weeks later. I did also attempt to raise the issue earlier here: https://discord.com/channels/916516304972824576/916713912970412103/966513513671565353 _was also the newest editor at the time, so I hope you can forgive me defering to a vetran ^^;;_ This does help add some context, thanks. I personally think that the appropriate action for you in this case would have been to tell Matt to bring it up with the other editors if he wanted to ignore the status quo behavior on this, though it does seem (from that snippet) that you pushed back on it a bit and merely were acknowledging that you aren't a dictator. Something something evil triumphs when good men do nothing. Though, I recognize that pragmatically this is a *really* blurry thing to implement in reality. I'll make sure to raise any contentious issues in a public channel going forward Like using `ERC-N`... 😠 I thought you favored switching to ERC-N in internal links? Nope EIP for everything There's even a lint in `eipw` for it! I appreciate you editing your comment btw ❤️ I'm about to go to bed, so I'll just leave some words that I've barely thought about so I'll have some interesting reading tomorrow morning. First, I don't think anyone involved needs an explicit punishment. In the grand scheme of things, considered solely on its own, this is a very insignificant dispute between editors over what digits to assign to a blob of text. Yes, it has implications, but at its core, it's basically nothing. I think the two things we need to do to improve the process here are: 1. From now on, discuss any potentially contentious actions in public, either here or in the ECH discord. Get participation from those you know feel strongly, and don't consider silence consent. Maybe put this in EIP-5069? 2. Add a rule explicitly prohibiting vanity EIP numbers to EIP-1, if it isn't already mentioned. hmm a rule that eip editors should not collude? I feel like if we need that rule then governance is already lost. that was my non-written point of the message :p I agree that the specific issue at hand is insignificant. If the issue at hand was somehow contained to that I would care far less. What concerns me far more is the *willingness* of editors to take an action that they almost certainly know is contentious among the editors at best and is against the de facto rules at worst. Worse, they did so in a way that appears to attempt to avoid/prevent engagement with the other editors (private conversations rather than public) implying intentional subversion. As Killari alluded to, if we have editors that are actively trying to subvert the system I don't think there exists any set of rules we could implement that would address the root problem. What we need are editors who don't try to subvert/game the system. This is certainly a hard problem, and one that every system of governance suffers from with with no known foolproof solution. We can create a bunch of rules that try to constrain the actions of the editors so they are limited in what they can do and there are well define grounds on which we can then exert punishment, but a clever editor who wants to subvert the rules will eventually find a way and we'll be right back in this situation again and again, constantly adding rules and complexity. For context, the two things I hate more than just about anything else in the world are bullies and people who abuse power, so this particular issue is certainly hitting me in a soft spot and possibly clouding my judgement (or giving clarity, if you agree that abuse of power is one of the worst sins imaginable). It has Read and Write. Hmm, I wonder why EIP-Bot can do it but your bot cannot then? Is the bot a GitHub App perhaps? They have different rights than actions. So far, https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/5275 is my only hope 😛 It seems to be an often requested feature, but no one has any idea how to make it work. Hm, no luck. This might be a workaround: https://stackoverflow.com/a/71683208 I don't think so? I think it is just a regular ol' GitHub action bot. Hm, it is using a different access token though. I could try that one? It isn't using the built-in GITHUB token? `eipw` is using: `${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}` EIP-Bot is using: `${{ secrets.TOKEN }}` This is why I wanted to delegate the GitHub side of things to someone else 😉 <@555483069038198827> when you get the chance, can you take a peek at https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/5240 ? Also, apologies for the open/close spam, but I'm also using the PR to test some build changes 😅 https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/5240#issuecomment-1186234078 🎉 What was the trick? Switching to a `pull_request_target` trigger instead of `pull_request`. The workflow definition comes from the base branch instead of the pull request so it gets a write token, or at least that's my understanding. Alright, someone needs to explain how this happened: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/runs/7373731082?check_suite_focus=true
